themes_detail.label: Street Condition Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints spiked to 40 THIS WEEK—a 611% jump from the 5.6-complaint weekly average—suggesting rapid deterioration of road infrastructure in Morrisania/Crotona that may pose safety and mobility risks.
evidence: 40 street condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 5.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (611% increase, z-score: 11.02)
Highest statistical anomaly in spike data, indicating acute, sustained deterioration
Concurrent Street Sweeping Complaint spike (3 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 avg, 700% increase)
reporting_angles: Document specific street locations with complaints; photograph potholes, crumbling curbs, or drainage issues
Interview residents about how street conditions are affecting commute, safety, and property damage; contact DOT about maintenance schedules

themes_detail.label: Rodent Infestation Uptick
themes_detail.summary: Rodent complaints jumped to 9 THIS WEEK—a 213% spike from the 2.9-complaint weekly average—indicating a possible infestation surge coinciding with street and sanitation stress in the district.
evidence: 9 rodent complaints THIS WEEK vs. 2.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (213% increase, z-score: 4.83)
Coincides with Street Sweeping Complaint spike (700%), suggesting sanitation breakdown may be attracting rodents
Aligns with 923 total unsanitary condition complaints over 90 days (third-highest category)
reporting_angles: Interview residents about sightings, health concerns, and property damage; map complaint locations to identify hotspots
Contact DSNY and Health Department about sanitation schedules and pest control response; investigate if staffing or street cleaning have declined

themes_detail.label: Illegal Animal Complaints Explode
themes_detail.summary: Illegal animal kept as pet complaints spiked to 4 LAST WEEK—a 3100% jump from the 0.1-complaint weekly average—suggesting a sudden emergence of animal welfare or public safety concerns.
evidence: 4 illegal animal kept as pet complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (3100% increase, z-score: 11.72)
Concurrent spike in animal-in-park complaints: 5 complaints last week vs. 0.9 avg (471% increase, z-score: 4.45)
Both spikes indicate concentrated animal-related incidents in narrow timeframe
reporting_angles: Identify specific animals involved and the neighborhoods/parks where complaints clustered; contact NYPD and Animal Care and Control
Interview residents about safety concerns and whether complaints relate to owner negligence or animal welfare crisis

themes_detail.label: Traffic Signal Failures Widespread
themes_detail.summary: Traffic signal condition complaints reached 63 TWO WEEKS AGO—a 331% spike from the 14.6-complaint weekly average—raising questions about transportation safety and DOT maintenance in the district.
evidence: 63 traffic signal complaints TWO WEEKS AGO vs. 14.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (331% increase, z-score: 4.1)
Suggests either widespread mechanical failure or deferred maintenance across multiple intersections
Correlates with elevated street condition complaints this week, indicating broader infrastructure stress
reporting_angles: Map complaint locations to identify which intersections have recurring signal issues; contact DOT for maintenance records and timeline
Interview residents and business owners about traffic congestion, safety incidents, and commute impacts from non-functional signals

themes_detail.label: Maintenance System Breakdown
themes_detail.summary: Maintenance or facility complaints spiked to 36 THREE WEEKS AGO—a 1957% jump from the 1.8-complaint weekly average (the highest z-score spike in the data at 19.98)—indicating potential systemic failure in building or infrastructure maintenance.
evidence: 36 maintenance or facility complaints THREE WEEKS AGO vs. 1.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (1957% increase, z-score: 19.98)—highest spike in dataset
Coincides with elevated heat/hot water complaints (3985 total over 90 days, highest category) suggesting building system failures
Pattern aligns with chronic community board budget requests for building and park reconstruction/upgrades, indicating longstanding neglect
reporting_angles: Identify which buildings or facilities generated the spike; obtain 311 complaint details to document what systems failed
Interview residents about conditions and response times; contact HPD and NYCHA (if applicable) about maintenance backlogs and staffing
